evals.prompt: I'm starting a new invite-only onboarding flow for our app. It needs clean business logic around invite states, a polished mobile-first UI, and exact implementation changes in the repo. You are the only agent currently running; start whatever other agent CLIs you need and handle this in the best way using the tools available.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps itself as conductor for the first planning pass, shows a short detected-tool summary plus recommended role map, uses brainstorming to split the work into small parallel slices, then launches specialist CLIs in tmux and routes results back through conductor check-ins.

evals.prompt: We need a billing settings redesign. I care about strong UX, clear plan-change and trial logic, and clean implementation without a lot of thrashing. Use Claude for exploration, Codex for implementation and code review, and Gemini for UI design unless one of them is missing. If the specialist panes are not already running, launch them.
evals.expected_output: The agent reflects the requested map back to the user, applies the sensible defaults where they match, reports any fallback substitutions if a preferred CLI is unavailable, and keeps ownership boundaries clear with conductor-led check-ins between rounds.

evals.prompt: Build a notifications preferences revamp with backend preference rules, cleaner responsive UI, and exact repo implementation. Move quickly and use the best agent workflow you have. Start by making the initial plan yourself, then spin up any other agents you need.
evals.expected_output: The agent defaults to role-based orchestration, keeps the invoking agent as conductor and first planner, prefers Claude for investigation, Codex for implementation and pure code-quality review, Gemini for UI design, and continues parallelizing implementation rounds with explicit conductor evaluation after each batch.

evals.prompt: Please tighten the spacing in the settings header and rename the primary button from 'Continue' to 'Save changes'.
evals.expected_output: The agent decides this task is too small for orchestration and stays single-threaded while saying why.

evals.prompt: I'm running this from Codex and want to stay the conductor myself. Use Gemini for UI design, Claude for repo exploration, and keep pure code-quality review separate from implementation when that helps. If one of those tools is missing, tell me the fallback before you start dispatching.
evals.expected_output: The agent preserves the invoking agent as conductor even though Codex is running the session, respects the user's custom role map, and reports any fallback substitutions before launching specialist panes.

evals.prompt: Use god-mode for a large feature. Prefer yolo or automatic proceed modes when the specialist CLIs support them. If a pane pauses waiting for permission to run a safe command, do not leave it stuck there.
evals.expected_output: The agent prefers `codex --yolo`, `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`, and `gemini --yolo` when available, classifies paused panes as `waiting-permission` versus `waiting-user`, auto-proceeds only clearly safe execution approvals with tmux key sends, and escalates risky prompts instead of blindly pressing Enter.

evals.prompt: Set up god-mode so specialist agents can notify the original orchestrator when they hit a permission gate or when they finish a batch. I want less manual polling and a cleaner callback loop.
evals.expected_output: The agent records the conductor pane ID, includes a `tmux-cli send "GODMODE ..." --pane=<conductor-pane>` callback protocol in kickoff prompts, and treats explicit `waiting-permission`, `waiting-user`, and `done` messages as first-class orchestration events.

evals.prompt: I'm installing god-mode into my agent setup and want to know where it should live and whether I should also install the Claude plugin wrapper for it.
evals.expected_output: The agent says `god-mode` is maintained only in `skills/god-mode/` as Playbooks-first skill content, does not present the Claude plugin wrapper as a maintained install path for this skill, and keeps any plugin-wrapper guidance limited to the other wrapper-backed skills.

evals.prompt: Use god-mode for a substantial feature and launch the specialist panes now. Do not stop to ask me for the exact startup text after the panes open.
evals.expected_output: The conductor launches each requested specialist CLI with a fully formed kickoff prompt already passed on the command line at launch time, instead of opening blank panes and relying on manual follow-up typing after startup.

evals.prompt: Use god-mode on this project. If the conductor or a specialist becomes unsure about a requirement or next step, I do not want anybody making up missing details.
evals.expected_output: The agent instructs confused specialists to ask back through the conductor and, when the conductor itself is unsure, asks the user instead of inventing requirements or guessing at missing constraints.

evals.prompt: Show me example specialist launch commands for Claude, Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode under god-mode. Include the exact prefixes you expect to use in launch snippets.
evals.expected_output: Every specialist launch example is prefixed with `env B2V_DISABLED=true`, such as `env B2V_DISABLED=true claude ...`, `env B2V_DISABLED=true codex ...`, `env B2V_DISABLED=true gemini ...`, and `env B2V_DISABLED=true opencode ...`.

evals.prompt: Use god-mode for a multi-step batch and assume one specialist pane hits an optional update prompt, release note screen, telemetry notice, or similar non-essential setup interruption before it can continue.
evals.expected_output: The conductor or specialist safely skips or dismisses the non-essential setup interruption, continues the assigned batch without stalling on optional prompts, and escalates through the conductor instead of guessing whenever the update appears required or the safety of skipping is unclear.
